extracted.intended_audience: Sage developers, Sage package maintainers, and downstream distribution maintainers (e.g., Linux distro packagers)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and requirements for preparing, patching, building, testing, and including SageMath packages (both upstream patches and downstream distribution packages), including rules for modularized distribution packages and dependency declarations.

rubrics_metrics.name: When to use patches vs modified tarballs
rubrics_metrics.description: Decide between maintaining patches or making a modified tarball.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use patches unless: you must change configure.ac or other autotools sources (or are autoconfiscating) — then make a modified tarball; the patch would be huge — make a modified tarball; upstream Makefile does not build shared libraries — autoconfiscate instead of patching. If upstream Makefile only hard-codes paths or flags, don't patch: override variables from the command line in spkg-install (example: $(MAKE) DESTDIR="$SAGE_ROOT/local").

rubrics_metrics.name: Preparing a patch by importing a GitHub pull request
rubrics_metrics.description: How to import an upstream GitHub PR as a patch file for Sage packages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fetch the PR as https://github.com/.../pull/N.patch and save it under patches/ with .patch extension. Update package-version.txt to indicate changed patch level so the package is rebuilt. Test building (make build) and expect 'Applying N.patch' messages; ignore safe fuzz/offset messages. Add the patch file to your branch, commit with a message like build/pkgs/NAME: Add https://.../pull/N as a patch; when opening your PR, CI will rebuild the patched package.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patch file format and header requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Patches must include documentation and have only one prefix level in paths.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A typical patch should have a title line, then a multi-line description (what the patch does, source, platform specifics, whether it should be pushed upstream). Diffs must have only one prefix level above the upstream source root (e.g., diff -dru Sphinx-1.2.2/file.orig Sphinx-1.2.2/file).

rubrics_metrics.name: Patch placement and conditional application
rubrics_metrics.description: Where to place patches and how to apply them conditionally.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Patches directly under patches/ are applied automatically before spkg-install if they have .patch extension. To apply patches conditionally (e.g., Solaris), place them in subdirectories of patches/ and call sage-apply-patches -d subdir from spkg-install. Example directory layout and spkg-install conditional: if [ $UNAME == "SunOS" ]; then sage-apply-patches -d solaris; fi

rubrics_metrics.name: Workflow for maintaining a set of patches
rubrics_metrics.description: Recommended git workflow to maintain patches against upstream.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fork/import upstream repo as branch 'upstream'. Create a branch for Sage changes, e.g., sage_package_VERSION. Make changes and commit. Generate patches with git format-patch -o SAGE_ROOT/build/pkgs/PACKAGE/patches/ upstream (remove and recreate patches/ first). Optionally create spkg-src to regenerate patch directory. When upstream updates, rebase your sage branch onto updated upstream and regenerate patches.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commit message practice for adding patches
rubrics_metrics.description: How to write commit messages when adding patch files to the package branch.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use commit messages like build/pkgs/PACKAGE: Add https://github.com/OWNER/REPO/pull/N as a patch so automatic tooling and CI can identify the change.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include patch files in package versioning
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure package-version.txt reflects changes when adding patches.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Modify package-version.txt to indicate the changed patch level so the package will be rebuilt even if upstream version did not change; important for testing and for others to see that the package changed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Automatic application of patches (file extension requirement)
rubrics_metrics.description: Patches are applied automatically only if placed under patches/ with .patch extension.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure browser-saved PR patches have .patch; rename if saved as .patch.txt. Patches without .patch may not be applied automatically.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion procedure for new and updated packages
rubrics_metrics.description: How to propose new packages or updates to Sage distribution (optional -> standard).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Open a GitHub PR labeled c: packages: experimental or c: packages: optional for optional/experimental inclusion. After a period without problems, propose standard inclusion with PR labeled c: packages: standard and make a proposal in the sage-devel Google Group. Upgrading packages or adding patches also requires opening a PR in the proper category.

rubrics_metrics.name: License information requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Where and how to record license information for Sage packages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Put license information both in SPKG.rst and in SAGE_ROOT/COPYING.txt. On upgrades, check whether the license changed between versions. If an upstream tarball cannot be redistributed, rename it to include 'do-not-distribute' to prevent mirror uploads. If some parts are free and others non-free, consider making a custom tarball with only free parts (see giac example).

rubrics_metrics.name: Prerequisites for new standard packages
rubrics_metrics.description: Requirements a package must meet to become part of Sage's standard distribution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Package must have a license compatible with GPLv3; build on fully supported platforms (Linux, macOS) and be installable from source or as a Python wheel; be of sufficient quality vs alternatives, justified by the authors; have spent time as optional (unless good reason); and be refereed per The Sage Repository on GitHub. Quality criteria include speed, documentation, usability, absence of memory leaks, maintainability, portability, and reasonable build time/size/dependencies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dependency declaration locations and types
rubrics_metrics.description: Where dependencies are declared and the kinds of dependencies Sage uses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The definitive list is in pyproject.toml. Sections include build-system.requires (Python packages needed for building), project.dependencies (runtime Python packages), project.optional-dependencies (optional features), external.build-requires and external.host-requires (system deps for building), and external.dependencies (runtime system libraries). External section uses PURLs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Downstream packaging build procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: Steps for downstream maintainers to build and package Sage for redistribution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 1) Obtain source (git clone or sdist). 2) Prepare clean build environment with required system libs and Python packages. 3) Build a wheel: python -m build --wheel --no-isolation (optionally --skip-dependency-check and -Cbuild-dir=build for reproducible builds). 4) Install the wheel: python -m installer --destdir="<pkgdir>" dist/sagemath-*.whl. 5) Test the build: python -m sage.doctest --all (note some tests may be known to fail). Contribute back issues/patches to SageGitHub if beneficial.

rubrics_metrics.name: Package naming conventions for downstream
rubrics_metrics.description: Suggested naming for downstream packages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use 'sagemath' or 'python-sagemath' if the distribution has a Python package naming convention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Modularized distribution: distribution naming and scope
rubrics_metrics.description: How to name distribution packages that provide modules in the sage.* namespace or not.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distributions that provide sage.* modules should be named sagemath-DISTRIBUTION (prefer dashes). Distributions that provide functionality not needing sage namespace should be positioned in general Python ecosystem (e.g., pplpy, memory-allocator) and not use sage namespace.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ordinary packages vs implicit namespace packages
rubrics_metrics.description: Constraint that ordinary packages (with __init__.py) cannot be split across distributions; use implicit namespace packages when splitting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Remove __init__.py to create implicit namespace packages (PEP 420) so modules with a common prefix can be included in multiple distributions. When making implicit namespace packages, __init__.py cannot be used for initialization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Source directory contents for distribution packages
rubrics_metrics.description: Files required/expected in the source directory of a distribution package.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each distribution package source dir (e.g., SAGE_ROOT/pkgs/sagemath-standard) should contain: sage (relative symlink to SAGE_ROOT/src/sage/), MANIFEST.in (controls included files; keep in sync with # sage_setup directives), pyproject.toml, setup.cfg, requirements.txt, README.rst, LICENSE.txt (symlink to SAGE_ROOT/src), VERSION.txt (updated by release manager), setup.py, tox.ini. Use sage --fixdistributions to maintain directives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Versioning conventions for hotfixes and development releases
rubrics_metrics.description: How to mark hotfixes and dev releases in version numbers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hotfixes: add suffix .post1, .post2 (PEP 440). Development increments: use anticipated next dev release number with .dev1, .dev2 etc. Examples: 9.7.beta8.post1 for hotfix; 9.7.beta9.dev1 for a dev increment. After merge, versions are synchronized.

rubrics_metrics.name: Declaring build-time dependencies
rubrics_metrics.description: How to declare build-time dependencies for distribution packages with Cython/C/C++ libraries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use pyproject.toml [build-system] requires to declare build-time Python package dependencies. C/C++ libraries cannot be declared via pyproject; ensure build environment provides necessary C/C++ libraries or include them in the distribution being built.

rubrics_metrics.name: Declaring run-time dependencies
rubrics_metrics.description: How to declare runtime dependencies for distribution packages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Declare run-time dependencies in setup.cfg as install_requires. If module-level imports pull in other packages at import time, those packages must be provided by the distribution or declared as runtime dependencies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reducing build-time and run-time dependencies
rubrics_metrics.description: Strategies to minimize unnecessary dependencies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reduce build-time deps by refactoring modules to smaller pieces or move some deps to runtime. Reduce module-level runtime deps by avoiding imports from *.all modules, replace module-level imports with method-level imports, use lazy_import() for on-demand imports, and avoid importing heavy classes just for isinstance checks — instead provide abstract base classes (ABCs) in lightweight modules and use isinstance against ABCs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Modularization anti-pattern and recommended alternative
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid importing classes just to run isinstance tests causing heavy dependencies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Anti-pattern: importing heavy class (pAdicFieldGeneric) for isinstance tests. Instead provide an abstract base class in a light-dependency module (sage.rings.abc) and use isinstance(object, sage.rings.abc.pAdicField) to avoid heavy imports. This may incur a small performance penalty but reduces dependency weight.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling optional functionality dependencies
rubrics_metrics.description: When to declare optional runtime dependencies vs leaving them optional for users.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a method needing an import provides core functionality, declare a runtime dependency; if it provides optional functionality, do not declare it and let the user install the extra distribution. Use extras_require in setup.cfg to declare optional dependencies (e.g., pip install sagemath-coding[symbolics]).

rubrics_metrics.name: Doctest-only dependencies and conditional doctests
rubrics_metrics.description: How to handle doctest dependencies so distributions can be tested separately.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use # optional or # needs doctest tags (Feature names like sage.symbolic) to mark doctests that depend on optional functionality. Tools rewrite tags to convention (use # needs for features present in default install). Use extras_require for doctest-only dependencies so developers can test distribution without full Sage present.

rubrics_metrics.name: Feature naming for doctest conditionalization
rubrics_metrics.description: Choose feature names that hide implementation details for maintainability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Define features that express capability, not implementation. Example: use sage.rings.finite_rings (which implies PARI) instead of sage.libs.pari. Mark doctests # needs sage.rings.finite_rings to express intent and reduce maintenance when implementation changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Testing distribution packages (tox/venv approach)
rubrics_metrics.description: Distribution packages must be testable separately using virtual environments and tox.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Create wheels (make wheels) to populate venv/var/lib/sage/wheels. Use tox to create disposable virtualenvs that install only the distribution to be tested and its Python deps. Each distribution provides tox.ini. Example invocation: ./bootstrap && ./sage -sh -c '(cd pkgs/sagemath-standard && SAGE_NUM_THREADS=16 tox -v -v -v -e sagepython-sagewheels-nopypi)'. The virtualenv is created under pkgs/<dist>/.tox/ and can be used to run a separate Sage installation for testing. The .tox directory can be deleted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distribution packages must be testable separately
rubrics_metrics.description: A requirement for modularized Sage distributions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distribution packages of the modularized Sage library must be testable separately while keeping integration testing with other portions of Sage. Use conditional doctests, extras_require, and tox virtualenvs to achieve this.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use provided tools for fixing distribution directives and doctests
rubrics_metrics.description: Tools exist to help maintain distribution directives and doctest tags.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use sage --fixdistributions to update distribution directives in source files (MANIFEST sync with # sage_setup directives). Use sage --fixdoctests to rewrite doctest tags according to conventions (# needs vs # optional).
